episodes.191301: On the late evening hours of June 28, storms brought severe wind to portions of Johnson and Miami Counties.
episodes.191303: Storms brought severe wind gusts to portions of Cass County in the late evening hours of June 28th. A lightning fatality was reported in Holden, MO, in Johnson County MO.
episodes.191316: Southwesterly surface winds ahead of an approaching cold front boosted dewpoints in the afternoon as high as 76 degrees at the Terre Haute and Indianapolis airports, and 77 degrees at Shelbyville.  Resulting CAPE of 2000-3000 J/kg initiated thunderstorms over east-central Illinois, which tracked eastward into west-central Indiana.  This cluster matured into a bow echo that produced a measured 68 mph gust at Crawfordsville before downing trees across the Indianapolis Metro, most notably the Beech Grove area.||The storms were maintained by 20-30 kts of 0-3 km wind shear, with wind damage reported through Rush County where several large trees were downed.  Anomalously high precipitable water values around 2.15 inches promoted isolated heavy rainfall of 2.00 to 2.30 inches from south of Crawfordsville to northern portions of the Indianapolis Metro, although antecedent abnormally dry conditions prevented any flooding.||Finally, an early evening landspout tornado crossed from Vermillion County, Illinois into Warren County, Indiana, while producing no damage along the second half (Indiana portion) of its entire 4.76-mile track, resulting in an EFU rating in Indiana.
episodes.191353: A burst of record level monsoonal moisture flowed into NM coupled with a backdoor frontal boundary moving through eastern NM. This yielded scattered to numerous afternoon thunderstorms developing over the high terrain of central and western NM on June 29th. One batch developed directly over the new South Fork burn scar along the Lincoln and Otero County line just west of Ruidoso. This storm expanded in coverage eastward toward Alto and Ruidoso, producing burn scar flash flooding and debris flows throughout the area. Nearly all if not all drainages into the Rio Ruidoso exhibited thick debris flows through town, warranting an evacuation of the Upper Canyon area. Numerous streets and water crossings were inundated with debris flows and flash flooding. Emergency officials reported there being 26 swift water rescues in Ruidoso on June 29th with zero injuries or fatalities. Heavy rains spread into the Rio Grande Valley and East Mountain Communities that evening. The torrential downpours produced 1 to 2 inches of rainfall over the ABQ metro in as little as one hour resulting in flash flooding across town. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities thankfully. Heavy rains returned to the Ruidoso area on June 30th in the form of storms anchored over the high terrain. Rainfall totals were estimated to be as high as 4 to 6 inches over portions of the Salt burn scar located just south of the Otero County line. Flash flooding and debris flows drained northward into Ruidoso and Ruidoso Downs to Hollywood. Another flash flood emergency was issued as a result and the torrential debris flows raged through U.S. Highway 70 with the worst of it focused near the Sudderth Drive intersection. Multiple vehicles were swept away, including a semi-truck. A sharp rise on the Rio Ruidoso was recorded reaching Minor flood stage again, just as it did on the 29th. Damage to businesses and the Ruidoso Hospital were reported.
episodes.191434: A surface warm front stationed south in northern Maryland began moving northward into central Pennsylvania during the afternoon of June 29, 2024 and continued progressing north through the evening hours. Ample instability coupled with very favorable low-level shear parameters allowed for severe thunderstorms along and ahead of the warm front.
episodes.191455: Severe thunderstorms with lightning and damaging winds moved across central Missouri on June 29th.
episodes.191456: A few severe storms moved across southeast Kansas during the evening of June 29th.
episodes.191553: A supercell moved across parts of Lyon and Osage Counties on the evening of June 28. This storm produced three brief tornadoes,  as well as flash flooding and a larger area of scattered 70-85 mph straight-line winds.
episodes.191706: A solitary late-night thunderstorm turned out to be one of the most prolific hail producers of the season in south central Nebraska.||The storm erupted in Lincoln County and then rolled east-southeast across Dawson County. Satellite and ground truth observations suggested approximately 150 square miles of wind and hail impacts along the storm���s path. The town of Gothenburg (and locations to the north of town) got the ball rolling with reports of 2.75��� diameter hail across the north side of town causing damage to windows, roofs, siding and vehicles. A 70 mph wind gust was measured on the Nebraska State Mesonet System at Wild Horse Golf Course. However, the community of Cozad took the brunt of the beastly supercell. Hail up to 4��� in diameter pummeled the town and left very few structures spared from damage. Cozad Community Hospital diverted patients to other facilities, temporarily closed the front entrance and lost all phone lines as the storm roared through. The Cozad City Pool was forced to close. Hail, wind and water damage occurred at Cozad Public Schools during an ongoing renovation. Damage to the auditorium and offices resulted in the need for alternative student and staff space for several weeks into the school year. One injury was reported to a person who was caught outside, sustaining cuts, bruises and losing consciousness. The thunderstorm moved southeast and slid just southwest of Lexington before dying out in northern Phelps county. Tens of millions of dollars of property and crop damage occurred along the thunderstorm���s 27-mile long path.||A couple hours later, isolated thunderstorms in Sherman, Buffalo and Hall counties produced 65 mph winds and hail near Ravenna and north of Wood River. Crop damage and downed power lines were reported.||The thunderstorm formed along a sagging frontal boundary. Mid-level lapse rates were steep in the region and low-level moisture convergence increased along the front.  The supercell formed on the tail end of a short wave traversing the Dakotas, likely owing its high intensity to the favorable right-rear region of a 300 MB jet streak to the northeast providing strong upper diffluence in the area. Though instability was clearly available with MUCAPE values of 2500 J/kg, a warm layer in the middle atmosphere was a limiting factor to more widespread storm coverage in the area.||The Storm Prediction Center included a large part of Nebraska in a Slight Risk for severe weather highlighted the potential for large hail in southwest Nebraska. However, due to the limited coverage of the severe weather, no watches were issued.
episodes.191809: Scattered thunderstorms developed as a low pressure system moved through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.192152: Increasing instability and strong deep layer shear along a cold front moving through the area spawned severe thunderstorms over Luce County on the afternoon of the 29th.
episodes.192304: An outflow boundary from previous convection across the Mississippi River Valley triggered scattered thunderstorms across south-central Illinois during the late morning and early afternoon of June 29th.  One of the cells produced wind damage in Toledo in Cumberland County, which resulted in one injury.
episodes.192365: A potent cold front approached the region during the afternoon/evening of the 29th. This resulted in the development of a line of scattered thunderstorms over northern Michigan during the afternoon into evening hours. One stronger storm at the southern end of the line periodically took on supercell tendencies as it crossed over Traverse City and tracked along M-72 through Kalkaska and Grayling. This resulted in up to dime size hail and wind damage near Williamsburg. Storms continued to produce some gusty winds across northeast Lower Michigan into Lake Huron.
episodes.192525: During the late afternoon to early evening of the 29th a line of storms formed along a stationary boundary running along the southern bank of the Canadian River Valley in the Texas Panhandle. One supercell was able to form off of this line and first produced an estimated 80-85 mph wind gusts in Carson County as it knocked over nine power poles along HEY207. As this supercell matured it moved north into Hutchinson County where it caused more wind damage but also hail up to 1.5��� in diameter.
episodes.192609: Scattered thunderstorms developed near a surface front across northern Oklahoma during the early evening of the 29th. Sufficient deep-layer wind shear and instability promoted an environment capable of transiently organized thunderstorms. A few such storms developed across north-central Oklahoma, producing reports of large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.192810: A low pressure system swept across eastern North Dakota and northwestern Minnesota in the evening hours of the 28th. Severe risks were hail and wind, and all of reports received were hail and wind related.
episodes.192813: A low pressure system swept across eastern North Dakota and northwestern Minnesota in the evening hours of the 28th. Severe risks were hail and wind, and all of reports received were hail and wind related.
episodes.192826: A cold front moved across the area on the evening of June 28th. Convection developed quickly along the front as the cap eroded, initially discrete but quickly growing upscale. Robust CAPE exceeding 3000 J/kg was in place with good directional shear to support rotating updrafts. This resulted in a handful of weak tornadoes in Cass county at the onset of storm development. After storms grew upscale they remained sub-severe.
episodes.192971: In the midst of abnormally hot conditions around the region, strong to severe thunderstorms thrived across West Virginia on June 29th and 30th. On both days, storms initially developed during peak heating hours and progressed through the state before diminishing with the loss of daytime heating. Storm damage was mainly observed in the form of downed trees each day.
episodes.192992: Scattered thunderstorms developed as a low pressure system moved through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.193220: A lone supercell thunderstorm developed just to the east of North Platte. As it tracked to the east southeast, it produced hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter northeast of Brady.
episodes.193230: An upper high was located over northeast Texas with modest low and mid level moisture brought into the Borderland on southeast winds.  Dew point depressions over the lowlands were still around 50 degrees supporting strong downburst winds with the strongest thunderstorms that developed.
episodes.193263: A complex of strong thunderstorms developed over western Pinal County, particularly in the area between Casa Grande and Arizona City, during the late afternoon into the early evening hours. The overall environment the thunderstorms developed under was characterized by weak to moderate instability with CAPE values ranging between 500-1000 J/KG and DCAPE values in excess of 1500 J/KG, which was favorable for strong to severe downburst winds to materialize.
episodes.193411: Scattered showers developed during the late afternoon and early evening along a slow-moving cold front that was draped from northern Indiana to near the I-72 corridor in central Illinois. Trained spotters reported that many of these showers exhibited weak rotation and brief funnel clouds, and one produced a landspout tornado in Vermilion County, which eventually tracked into Indiana. This tornado was on the ground for a total of 15 minutes and was rated EF0 after producing minor tree damage.
episodes.193593: An area of low pressure moved through the Northland during the early morning hours of the 29th and brought a cluster of thunderstorms from Itasca County through the Minnesota Arrowhead. The storms had been severe west of Itasca County and were on a downward trend as the moved east. One last severe hail report was received from near Inger where quarter sized hail was reported.
episodes.193807: A warm and moist airmass was ushered in after a warm front passed. A few strong to severe thunderstorms developed in portions of Pennsylvania, producing damaging wind gusts which knocked down trees and a few wires.
episodes.193865: Lingering sub-tropical moisture remained across western Colorado with drier air pushing in from the west as the high pressure shifted further east with drier air increasing aloft. This resulted in less coverage of storms but some storms were still capable of producing brief heavy rain, one of which resulted in some street flooding in Garfield County.
episodes.193900: Low pressure moving across the upper Great Lakes resulted in broad and deep warm, very moist southerly flow throughout the Ohio Valley and lower Great Lakes regions. A cold front with an attendant shortwave crossed the region, resulting in showers and thunderstorms. Joint probability was 60-90% for >1000 J/kg SBCAPE and >30 kt of shear, with the bulk shear packed into the lowest levels in the 25-35 knot range. Convection held off until late afternoon / early evening due to cloud cover limiting insolation and surface-based instability earlier in the day.
episodes.193901: Low pressure moving across the upper Great Lakes resulted in broad and deep warm, very moist southerly flow throughout the Ohio Valley and lower Great Lakes regions. A cold front with an attendant shortwave crossed the region, resulting in showers and thunderstorms. Joint probability was 60-90% for >1000 J/kg SBCAPE and >30 kt of shear, with the bulk shear packed into the lowest levels in the 25-35 knot range. Convection held off until late afternoon / early evening due to cloud cover limiting insolation and surface-based instability earlier in the day.
episodes.194013: Scattered severe thunderstorms tracked across south central and southeast Kansas beginning during the afternoon hours of the 29th and lasting into the late evening hours. These storms produced quarter to baseball sized hail and damaging wind gusts up to 75 mph; damage occurred to trees and power poles. There was one landspout reported inear Yates Center. Heavy rain persisted over south central Kansas which led to flash flooding in Kingman.
episodes.194618: At the surface, a wavy warm front swept eastward from Lake Michigan, southern Lower MI, and western OH to southern Lake Huron, southwestern ON, eastern Lake Erie, and northwestern PA as an occluded low drifted from central Lake Superior to central ON during the mid-morning through early afternoon hours of the 29th. Multiple lines of multicell showers and thunderstorms developed and persisted generally eastward along and ahead of the surface warm front amidst weak to moderate MUCAPE and DCAPE, respectively, and moderate to strong effective bulk shear. A very brief mesovortex-related tornado occurred in Huron County, amidst surface-based effective storm-relative helicity near 150 to nearly 200 meters squared per second squared and mixed layer LCL's between 750 meters and 1000 meters AGL. Isolated straight-line convective wind damage impacted Lorain and Cuyahoga Counties.
episodes.194619: At the surface, a wavy warm front swept eastward from Lake Michigan, southern Lower MI, and western OH to southern Lake Huron, southwestern ON, eastern Lake Erie, and northwestern PA as an occluded low drifted from central Lake Superior to central ON during the mid-morning through early afternoon hours of the 29th. Multiple lines of multicell showers and thunderstorms developed and persisted generally eastward along and ahead of the surface warm front amidst weak to moderate MUCAPE and DCAPE, respectively, and moderate to strong effective bulk shear. One of the lines of showers and thunderstorms produced a gale-force convective wind gust along the Lorain County shore in northern OH.
episodes.194622: At the surface, a wavy warm front swept eastward from Lake Michigan, southern Lower MI, and western OH to southern Lake Huron, southwestern ON, eastern Lake Erie, and northwest PA as an occluded low drifted from central Lake Superior to central ON during the mid-morning through early afternoon hours of the 29th. Multiple lines of multicell showers and thunderstorms developed and persisted generally eastward along and ahead of the surface warm front in northwest PA during the early afternoon. These storms occurred amidst weak to moderate MUCAPE and DCAPE, respectively, and moderate to strong effective bulk shear. Isolated straight-line convective wind damage occurred in the Meadville area.
episodes.204616: During the afternoon and evening hours of June 28th, storms brought severe weather to portions of NW and western Missouri. Additionally, around 11 pm on June 28th, a lightning strike killed a 53 year old man at the Holden Rodeo.

Heavy rain totaling 1.48 inches at the Cow Mountain RAWS station and radar estimated to be higher than 2 inches over the recent South Fork burn scar produced life threatening and extremely dangerous debris flows down Cedar Creek just north of Ruidoso. This torrent raged through town overtopping several bridges and crossings including, Mechem Road (NM Highway 48), Paradise Canyon Road, Cree Meadows Road, and Wiley Road. The debris flow also overtopped a small dam near Cree Meadows Road. Fire crews were pulled out of sensitive areas due to the threat of heavy rains and an evacuation order was issued for the Village of Ruidoso just after 4pm MDT. Some people became trapped in their vehicle along Paradise Canyon Road, requiring swift water rescue. This one swift water rescue was one of a total of 26 swift water rescues for the day caused by the flash flooding and debris flow that occurred across the Village of Ruidoso. Miraculously, there were no reports of injuries or fatalities. Damage is an estimate based on cars and road crossings being involved.

Heavy rains over the recent South Fork burn area totaling up to 1.48 inches at the Cow Mountain RAWS and estimate by radar to have surpassed 2 inches caused flash flooding heavy debris flows along the Rio Ruidoso. This torrent impacted several bridges and water crossings including, N. Eagle Drive, Grindstone Canyon Road, Country Club Drive. Numerous homes were impacted with a total of 26 swift water rescues stretched across the Rio Ruidoso and Cedar Creek drainages through the Village of Ruidoso. Fire crews were pulled out of sensitive areas due to the threat of heavy rains and an evacuation order was issued for the Village of Ruidoso shortly after 4pm MDT. The debris flow eventually reached downstream past the Village of Ruidoso to the Ruidoso Downs Track overtopping the edge of the facility and flowing out over the track. For reference, the Ruidoso Downs Track was constructed over the Rio Ruidoso. Miraculously there were no reports of injuries or fatalities. Damage is an estimate based extent and limited information.

Flash flooding and a debris flow was reported in Eagle Creek within the new South Fork burn area crossing NM Highway 532 (Ski Run Road) between mile markers 2 and 3. This debris flow was reported to have reached the Alto Reservoir, overtopping the diversion channel. The Cow Mountain RAWS near the headwaters of Eagle Creek recorded 1.48 inches of total rainfall this day. Damage from this individual event is unknown. However, there were more impactful debris flows and flash flooding within the South Fork burn scar further south and through Ruidoso.

A storm chaser monitored a landspout tornado that maintained connection to the ground for much of its entire 4.76 mile track from far eastern Illinois into Indiana.  The landspout started in Vermillion County, IL (in NWS Lincoln's area) at 1815 EST and crossed into Warren County, IN at 1823 EST.  Minor EF0 damage was observed 750 feet west of the state line in Illinois, nonetheless the landspout was rated EFU along the entirety of the 2.25-mile (Indiana) portion of its track in Warren County where no damage was observed.
